title: Maximum of three
instructorPromptText: Write a program that asks the user for three numbers, then prints the largest one. Do not use the built-in max() — decide with conditionals.

specGateDimensions.description: Are the three numbers read as integers, floats, or either? The spec should commit to a type so the input() calls can be cast accordingly.
specGateDimensions.rationale: Students often leave input as strings and get lexicographic comparison bugs (e.g. '9' > '100' is True). Naming the type up front prevents this.

specGateDimensions.description: What should the program print when two or three of the numbers are equal to the maximum (e.g. 5, 5, 3 or 7, 7, 7)? Is printing that shared value once the correct behavior?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Ties are the classic hidden case in max-of-N. Committing to 'print the value' vs 'announce a tie' makes the conditional structure deterministic.

specGateDimensions.description: What exactly is printed — just the number, or a sentence like 'The largest is 7'?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Phase 4 needs a concrete expected output to diff against; 'prints the largest' is underspecified.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program assume the user enters valid numbers, or does it handle non-numeric input (e.g. via try/except)? Either commitment is acceptable.
specGateDimensions.rationale: At unit_2 both 'assume valid input and let it crash' and 'wrap in try/except' are legitimate; forcing the student to name the choice prevents silent drift.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student forgets to cast input() to int/float and compares strings, producing wrong results on multi-digit inputs like '9' vs '100'

Chained conditional misses a branch — e.g. checks `if a > b and a > c` and `elif b > c` but never handles the case where c is largest, or uses `>` everywhere so ties fall through to an unreachable else
Spec commits to handling ties explicitly, but code uses strict `>` comparisons so one of the tied branches is silently skipped
Plan describes nested if/elif on all three variables; code introduces a `largest` accumulator variable and compares it against each input in sequence — coherent alternative structure
Plan uses separate if statements; code collapses into a single if/elif/else chain — coherent simplification
Output format committed in spec (e.g. full sentence) but code prints the bare number, or vice versa
